readme: Golden cases for billing/planning/map_links.py (L1). Every number is written out. `parse` cases: the text, then either the two numbers kept to six decimals or the refusal sentence. `map_link` and `directions` cases: the place(s) and the exact URL, or null.

parse.why: The common form: 48.2082, 16.3738 is latitude 48.208200 and longitude 16.373800.
A space between the two numbers: 48.2082 16.3738.
German decimal commas with a semicolon: 48,2082; 16,3738 is 48.2082 and 16.3738.
Decimal commas AND a comma between them: 48,2082, 16,3738.
A map's right-click pair, 48.20817433281537, 16.37381946802135, kept to six decimals half-up: 48.208174 and 16.373819.
Signs are kept: -33.8688 is inside -90..90 and -151.2093 inside -180..180, so the pair is accepted.
San Francisco pasted longitude first: -122.4194 is not a latitude (outside -90..90), and 37.7749 would be one, so the sentence says the longitude came first.
parse.refusal: The latitude -122.4194 is outside -90 to 90. It looks like the longitude came first: the latitude goes first. For example 48.2082, 16.3738.

parse.why: 99, 16: a latitude of 99 does not exist.
parse.refusal: The latitude 99 is outside -90 to 90. It looks like the longitude came first: the latitude goes first. For example 48.2082, 16.3738.

parse.why: 48.2, 200: a longitude of 200 does not exist (and 200 is no latitude either).
parse.refusal: The longitude 200 is outside -180 to 180. Check the second number, for example 48.2082, 16.3738.

parse.why: Only 48.2082: one number is half a pair.
parse.refusal: These coordinates have only one number. Paste a latitude and a longitude, for example 48.2082, 16.3738.

parse.why: An address is not a pair: its only number, 23, is one number.
parse.refusal: These coordinates have only one number. Paste a latitude and a longitude, for example 48.2082, 16.3738.

parse.why: 48.2 16.3 12: three numbers are not a pair.
parse.refusal: These coordinates could not be read. Paste two numbers, the latitude first, for example 48.2082, 16.3738.
There are no coordinates here. Paste a latitude and a longitude, for example 48.2082, 16.3738.

map_link.why: Coordinates 48.208200 / 16.373800 become query=48.2082,16.3738 (comma encoded as %2C, trailing zeros dropped).
When both exist the coordinates are used, not the address: 48.2207, 16.3477 and not Währinger Gürtel.
Only a latitude (an inconsistent record) is not a position: the address is used.
Street, second line, 1090 Wien, AT; umlauts as UTF-8 percent codes, spaces as %20, commas as %2C.
No coordinates and no address: no link at all.

directions.why: From a hotel's coordinates 48.1986, 16.3417 to a studio's address Hauptstraße 1, 2340 Mödling, AT.
The destination has nothing to point at: no link.
The origin has nothing to point at: no link.
